## Answer

- **No set of documents sums to R9,649.56.** The exact-sum search (section 15 Order B step 1) over 30 document options dated 2024-10-01 to 2025-01-31 (whole documents and their gas / deposit parts, sets of up to 6, tolerance 0.02) found **0** set(s); 0 of them use only documents that were dated on or before 30 Dec 2024 and not already settled by a same-amount payment. The wider pass (2024-07-01 to 2025-03-31, 61 options, sets of up to 4) found 0. PROVEN (search output below). So the premise that the payment is an exact sum of documents fails for 35877; the premise that the customer pays whole invoices survives in a narrower form: the payment names and covers one whole invoice (39311) and overpays it.
- **R9,649.56 is 39311's net gas amount grossed up by 15% VAT a second time:** R8,390.92 x 1.15 = R9649.558, which rounds to R9,649.56. The excess, R1,258.64, is exactly 15% of R8,390.92. Arithmetic PROVEN; that the payer added VAT to a VAT-inclusive amount is ASSUMED (it is the only arithmetic that reproduces the figure to the cent, and the bank line names only 39311). R8,390.92 already includes VAT (database header 39311: excl 13,896.45 + VAT 2,084.47 = 15,980.92 before credit note 11573's -7,590.00).
- **The ERP did not leave the excess unallocated; the earlier "database records only -8,390.92" compared one slice only.** The database holds 35877 as 3 ref slices plus a zero-net Alloc mirror (0.00): 8,390.92 to 39311, 851.02 to 34831, 407.62 to 41238 = **9,649.56**, equal to the TXT. The R1,258.64 excess was spread by the ERP cashier as R851.02 to invoice 34831 and R407.62 to invoice 41238 (an invoice dated 5 Mar 2025, so a later reallocation; that slice comes from the `DTRX2603.TXT` load). PROVEN as database content; per section 15 ERP payment tagging is corroboration, never proof of what the customer intended.
- **Where the ~R407.6 credit comes from.** R1,258.64 less the R851.00 legacy Part 1B deposit balance is R407.64 on the statement basis; the ERP itself applied exactly R407.62 of 35877 to 41238. The ERP tags show the R851.02 reaching the legacy pre-2024 cylinder documents by a two-step route: payment 32620 (5 Aug 2024, R7,437.11 = invoice 34831 in full) was sliced R6,586.09 to 34831 plus a net R851.02 to six 2022-2023 cylinder/EMPTIES documents (12454, 13956, 16770, 17259, 23253, 23259), leaving 34831 R851.02 short, and 35877 then cleared that R851.02. So in the ERP's allocation the R851.02 legacy deposit residual has been paid with cash, while the statements route all payments to Part 1A and keep the R851.00 open in Part 1B. ASSERTED (ERP tagging, untrusted on its own).
- **Classification:** a genuine overpayment of R1,258.64 (section 13: log full cash, show the variance, carry the surplus), most likely a payer VAT error, not an exact sum of documents and not a mirror carry. Confidence: **high** that no document set explains it (PROVEN search), **medium** for the VAT gross-up reading (it reproduces the figure to the cent and no innocent goods combination does, but 15% coincidences occur on this account (section 2) and no remittance confirms it), **low** that the customer meant to pay the legacy R851.02 (it does not explain the R407.62 remainder).
